_note: One creator's public tier list for bits, shown on a bit's detail sheet under a credit link. Not BeyClub's writing and not one of the three ranking sources — display only, it never reaches blendRating(). `bits` holds the catalogue codes the entry covers; it is a list because the video rates all six gear bits together. `at` is the point in the video, in seconds, and becomes a ?t= deep link. `note` is one trimmed sentence, at most 140 characters — the detail sheet is already long and this section is meant to stay three lines. The sheet lists NR/Nr and OP/Op as separate rows on different grades; they are one physical part, so loadCatalogue() hands the same pick to both casings.

credit.author: ToxicShark
credit.sourceName: Ranking EVERY Bit In Beyblade X

picks.note: Single-handedly elevates left-spin blades through spin equalization, and finishes well on spin.
Top-tier stamina — keeps more spin on the rails than Ball, and is safer to hard-launch in Rod mirrors.
The best stamina bit among the high burst-resistance options; it tanks hits and stabilizes well.
The longest spin time of any aggressive balance bit, and a versatile anti-attack pick under top-heavy CX combos.
Arguably the best bit in the game once mastered — exceptional endgame stamina and KO power, high skill ceiling.
Extremely consistent and highly controlled attack, with low gears and solid endgame stamina.
The former number one and still a top stamina pick, though Free Ball is safer on the rails.
Aggressive with enough LAD to outspin attack types, but it bleeds stamina on the rail if misplayed.
Stationary stamina and defense — a lower centre of gravity and smaller contact patch grip the stadium well.
A more aggressive Rush, but the launch tech is harder and the result more volatile.
A smaller face than Flat preserves more energy on the rails, but the top attack bits outclass it.
Low rail stamina loss and high ratchet burst resistance, though it spun shorter than Free Ball in testing.
The classic balance bit that once won tournaments, now outclassed by Kick, Level and Jolt.
Terrible brand new, but a strong counter-attacker with good grip and stamina once worn down.
Solid endgame stamina for a balance-attack bit, but the newer balance bits have passed it.
The lowest attack bit there is — useful for specific ratchet-sniper builds.
A stationary landmine bit that moves smoothly; good against inexperienced players, limited against pros.
A low gear count gives controlled rail movement, but it leans over and destabilizes.
A wider Point — it can outspin Cobalt Dragoon on Elevate with the right blade, but Point and Level are better.
Inconsistent and topples over easily; its wins are anomalies you cannot repeat.
A budget Rush replacement, but too fast with too many gears to control.
The extra bottom friction never turns into real defense and drains stamina quickly.
The early-game attack standard, now completely outclassed on stamina by modern attack bits.
Used briefly on Cobalt Dragoon for minor LAD before Elevate arrived, but its stamina is weak.
Noticeably worse than a standard Taper because of the raised centre of gravity.
A niche ratchet-sniper bit from an earlier meta with no competitive stamina left.
Gimmicky, prone to bursting, and outclassed on every metric.
Not bad in itself, just redundant next to Free Ball, Ball and Low Orb.
A height-adjustable Kick — raising the centre of gravity only makes it worse than standard Kick.
Its theoretical balance utility never shows up in results; Point and Kick outclass it.
A budget Rush alternative that lacks control and is heavily outclassed by Rush and Low Rush.
The wall ring adds no defense while adding burst risk and rail stamina drain.
Excessive gears kill stamina on the rail — strictly worse than Flat.
Drastically raises height and burst risk; the recent tournament wins are anomalies.
Extremely high burst risk and poor performance.
Hyper-volatile and prone to self-extremes — only worth it as a high-variance panic option for beginners.
The high centre of gravity destabilizes the bey and leaves the ratchet easy to snipe.
Uncontrollable movement and abysmal stamina.
Gimmicky and ineffective across almost every competitive build.
Banned from official tournament play because it damages stadium surfaces.
Stationary centre-docking with low burst resistance — an easy target for attack types.
The worst bit in the game; the jumping gimmick ruins both balance and stamina.
Stationary, with low burst resistance and poor stamina.
Inferior face geometry and needless height options make it worse than standard Point.
Horrible burst resistance, and the gimmick fires late when there is no energy left to KO with.
Low stability, high burst risk and terrible stamina.
Unbelievably loose in the ratchet — extremely burst-prone and unusable.
